title: Algebraic-space isomorphism functors for coherent families
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $f:X\to B$ be a finitely presented morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space, def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. Fibre products are sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. For an $S$-scheme $T$, let $\mathcal C(T)$ be the groupoid of pairs $(b:T\to B,M)$, where $M$ is a finitely presented quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_{X\times_BT}$-module, flat over $T$, with support proper over $T$. Here finite presentation means etale locally a cokernel of a map between finite rank free modules; flatness is stalkwise flatness over base local rings on etale charts [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over]; proper support means $M\simeq i_*N$ for a closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow X\times_BT$ with $Z\to T$ proper and $N$ finite type quasi-coherent [def-sfb-space-proper-quot-functor]. Modules and tensor pullback use [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module, def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. Arrows over $v:T\to T_1$ are isomorphisms $v_X^*M_1\simeq M$ with $b=b_1v$; composition uses canonical pullback composition isomorphisms. For every $S$-scheme $T$ and $x,y\in\mathcal C(T)$, the presheaf on $T$-schemes sending $a:T'\to T$ to $\operatorname{Isom}_{\mathcal C(T')}(a^*x,a^*y)$ is represented by an algebraic space over $T$. Equivalently, the diagonal of this fibred groupoid is representable by algebraic spaces [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids].

proof.text: Fix $x=(b:T\to B,M)$ and $y=(c:T\to B,N)$. Form the equality presheaf $E=h_T\times_{B\times_SB}B$, using $(b,c)$ and $\Delta_B$. Since $B$ is an algebraic space, its diagonal is representable by schemes [def-trf-algebraic-space], so $E$ is a scheme over $T$. Its universal property says that a map $a:T\prime\to T$ factors through $E$ exactly when $ba=ca$, and that the factorization is unique. The requisite products are sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Every isomorphism of the two pulled-back objects requires this equality of their maps to $B$, by the definition of arrows in $\mathcal C$. Thus their isomorphism presheaf has a canonical map to $E$; we will construct its representing space over $E$.

Write $e:E\to T$ and $d=be=ce:E\to B$. The two pullbacks of the underlying spaces are canonically $X_E=X\times_BE$, and the pulled-back modules are $M_E,N_E$. By [lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality], finite presentation of $f$ survives base change, first to $X\times_{B,b}T\to T$ and $X\times_{B,c}T\to T$, then to $X_E\to E$. In particular each of the first two maps is locally of finite type: on a chart a finite presentation of an algebra supplies finitely many algebra generators. Apply [lem-sfb-space-module-base-change-flat-proper-support] to each of these two maps and $e$. It gives that $M_E,N_E$ are quasi-coherent, finitely presented, flat over $E$, and have support proper over $E$. This uses arbitrary base change of modules, not flatness of $e$ or of $f$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-module-hom-affine] to $X_E\to E$ and to the ordered pairs $(M_E,N_E)$, $(N_E,M_E)$, $(M_E,M_E)$, $(N_E,N_E)$. The target module in each pair is finitely presented, flat over $E$, with support proper over $E$, as established above. Obtain representing algebraic spaces $H,H\prime,A,D$ over $E$ for these four Hom functors, with bijections natural on all schemes over $E$. We only need their algebraic-space representability; their affine and finite-presentation conclusions are stronger than needed here.

Let $P=H\times_EH\prime$ and $Q=A\times_ED$. On each scheme $U\to E$, define $k:P\to Q$ by $(u:M_U\to N_U,v:N_U\to M_U)\mapsto(vu,uv)$. Tensor pullback [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors] is a functor, so it preserves composition and identities; these formulas commute with restriction, hence define a natural transformation. As morphisms of algebraic spaces are precisely natural transformations [def-trf-algebraic-space], this is a morphism of spaces over $E$. The identities define a section $s:E\to Q$. Form $J=P\times_{Q,k,s}E$. All three fibre products in this construction are algebraic spaces by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. There is no need to prove that $s$ is a closed immersion, since the desired conclusion is only algebraic-space representability.

source.place: Tag 08K9 (proposition-isom), composition map and fibre-product construction; only representability is retained.

proof.text: The fibre-product description gives $J(U)=\{(u,v):vu=\operatorname{id}_{M_U},\ uv=\operatorname{id}_{N_U}\}$ for every $U\to E$. Projection to $u$ identifies this with $\operatorname{Isom}(M_U,N_U)$: its inverse assigns $(u,u^{-1})$, and an inverse is unique since $v=v(uv\prime)=(vu)v\prime=v\prime$. These bijections commute with pullback, which preserves identities and composites. For an arbitrary $a:T\prime\to T$, a map $T\prime\to J$ over $T$ first chooses its unique factorization through $E$, and then just such an isomorphism. If no factorization exists, both sets are empty. Thus $J\to E\to T$ represents the entire isomorphism presheaf in the statement, including when $b\ne c$.

Finally unpack the diagonal using the groupoid and 2-fibre-product conventions of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Its 2-base change along $(x,y):T\to\mathcal C\times_S\mathcal C$ has over $a:U\to T$ objects $(z,\alpha:z\xrightarrow{\sim}a^*x,\beta:z\xrightarrow{\sim}a^*y)$. Send this object to $\beta\alpha^{-1}$. Every isomorphism $\varphi:a^*x\to a^*y$ occurs using $(a^*x,\operatorname{id},\varphi)$; two triples with the same isomorphism have the unique compatible arrow $\alpha\prime^{-1}\alpha$ between them. This is an equivalence to the discrete groupoid of the isomorphism presheaf, natural in $U$. Since that presheaf is represented by $J$, every such 2-base change is an algebraic space. This proves precisely the diagonal formulation as well as its asserted equivalence.
